Combined astronomical test for several proxies and sections

Source: R/astro_sedrate_multi.R
astro_sedrate_multi.Rd

Runs astro_sedrate_test on every series (proxy) and fit and combines the evidence: within a section all series share one sedimentation rate, so their same-rate evidence is combined rate by rate; sections have their own rates and are combined at the end.

Usage

astro_sedrate_multi(
  data = NULL,
  section = NULL,
  sedmin = 1,
  sedmax = 20,
  numsed = 60,
  fit = c(1, 2),
  combine = c("minp", "stouffer"),
  scores = c("TimeOpt", "peaks"),
  weights = NULL,
  age_ma = NULL,
  targetE = NULL,
  targetP = NULL,
  targetO = NULL,
  n_null = 200,
  null_smooth = 2,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The series to test (named list; each element an evenly spaced two-column matrix or data frame with depth in metres in column 1 and proxy value in column 2). Series of the same section must share the depth scale. Unnamed elements are named "series1", "series2", ... Required, no default (Default=NULL gives an error).

section

Section label of every series (character or numeric vector, same length as data); series with the same label share one sedimentation rate and are combined rate by rate. NULL puts all series in one section. Default=NULL.

sedmin, sedmax

Lowest and highest trial sedimentation rate in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0): one value for all sections, or one value per section (named by section label, or in the order of unique(section)). Default=1 and Default=20.

numsed

Number of trial rates per section (integer, > 0), log-spaced unless linLog = 0 is passed through .... Default=60.

fit

TimeOpt fits run for every series (numeric vector with 1 (precession modulated by eccentricity), 2 (short eccentricity modulated by the 405-kyr cycle) or both); every fit of every series is a separate component. Default=c(1, 2).

combine

How the components of one section are combined at each rate (character): "minp" takes the best component, "stouffer" sums their correlation-corrected standard-normal scores (see Details). Default=c("minp", "stouffer"), i.e. "minp".

scores

Evidence used per series and fit, entered as separate components (character, one or both of "TimeOpt" (the TimeOpt significance S_opt) and "peaks" (the tuned-band peak score S_peaks)). Default=c("TimeOpt", "peaks").

weights

Weights of the series in the Stouffer combination (named numeric vector, names as in data); series not named get weight 1. NULL gives all series equal weight. Default=NULL.

age_ma

Age of the record in Ma (numeric) for the AstroGeo22 target periods; passed to astro_sedrate_test. NULL uses present-day periods. Default=NULL.

targetE, targetP, targetO

Your own eccentricity, precession and obliquity target periods in kyr (numeric vectors), passed to astro_sedrate_test; NULL uses the La2004/AstroGeo22 periods. Default=NULL.

n_null

Number of noise series simulated per series and fit (integer, > 0); passed to astro_sedrate_test. Default=200.

null_smooth

Number of neighbouring rates on each side pooled for the same-rate p and smoothing of the noise statistics (integer, >= 0); passed to astro_sedrate_test and used for the combined score. Default=2.

run_multicore

Simulate the noise series in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE); passed to astro_sedrate_test. Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores for the parallel computation (integer); NULL chooses automatically (see astro_sedrate_test). Default=NULL.

verbose

Print a progress message for every series and fit (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

...

Further arguments passed to astro_sedrate_test, e.g. linLog, coco, tune or null_fit (not keep_null, sensitivity or target_sensitivity, which are set by this function).

Value

A list of class astro_sedrate_multi with

sections

per section: data frame of rate, combined score S_multi (-log10 same-rate p), same-rate p, family-wise p and the number of components used

best

per section: best rate, S_multi and family-wise p

components

per series and fit: best rate and family-wise p of its own score

p_all

Fisher combination of the section family-wise p-values

runs

the astro_sedrate_test results

Details

Which tests enter. For every series and fit the TimeOpt significance (S_opt) and the tuned-band peak score (S_peaks) of astro_sedrate_test enter as separate components (not their joint score, which loses power on short records); a component enters the combination at a rate only where it is testable there (enough samples per carrier cycle and enough modulating cycles after the edge trim). Tests that cannot work on a series (for example the 405-kyr fit on a record that spans fewer than two 405-kyr cycles at that rate) therefore do not dilute the evidence of the others. Weights can be given per series (for example to down-weight a proxy known to be diagenetically overprinted); they must be chosen before looking at the results.

Combination within a section. combine = "stouffer" sums the standard-normal scores of the same-rate p-values, z = sum(w z_i) / sqrt(w' R w), where R is the correlation between the components' z-curves over the testable rates (clamped to 0-1; proxies of one section share noise, and fit 1 and fit 2 of one proxy share data, so the components are not independent). This is the most powerful combination when several proxies carry the signal. combine = "minp" (default) takes the best component at each rate (most powerful when only some proxies or tests carry the signal, the usual case; it is calibrated with independent noise series per component and is therefore slightly conservative for correlated proxies). Either statistic is calibrated with the noise series of the components (same-rate p, rates within null_smooth steps pooled, exponential tail), and the family-wise p over the rates of the section uses the minimum-p method.

Combination of sections. Section-level family-wise p-values are combined with Fisher's method (sections are independent records): p_all.

Independent age control (biostratigraphic duration bounds, magnetostratigraphy, radioisotopic ages) is given through sedmin and sedmax per section; a narrower, independently justified range reduces the number of rates tested and so raises the attainable significance (Kemp, 2016).

References

Kemp, D.B. (2016). Optimizing significance testing of astronomical forcing in cyclostratigraphy. Paleoceanography 31, 1516-1531 <doi:10.1002/2016PA002963>

Stouffer, S.A., Suchman, E.A., DeVinney, L.C., Star, S.A. and Williams, R.M. (1949). The American Soldier, Vol. 1: Adjustment during Army Life. Princeton University Press.

Westfall, P.H. and Young, S.S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing: Examples and Methods for p-Value Adjustment. Wiley, New York, ISBN 978-0-471-55761-6.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d1 <- mag[1:300, ]
d2 <- cbind(d1[, 1], d1[, 2] + rnorm(300, sd = sd(d1[, 2])))
res <- astro_sedrate_multi(list(a = d1, b = d2), sedmin = 0.4, sedmax = 1.5, numsed = 12,
    fit = 1, n_null = 10, coco = FALSE)
res$best
#>   section best_sedrate  S_multi      p_fw n_series
#> 1       1     1.330168 1.321453 0.4545455        2
# }
